title: Exploring the Impact of Frontal Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation on Self-Harm Behavior in Adolescents
summary:
Background: Adolescence is a challenging time with many changes, and it's a period when psychiatric disorders can develop. Self-harm is common among teenagers and is a serious issue. Those who self-harm often have various psychiatric problems, making diagnosis difficult. Impulsivity and risk-taking are linked to self-harm, especially in teens aged 11 to 25. Problems with impulse control contribute to self-harm and suicidal behaviors. Improving impulse control might help reduce self-harm.

Method: This project will explore using transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), a non-invasive brain stimulation technique, to reduce self-harm in adolescents. In the first phase, 30 adolescents (11-17 years) with self-harm behavior will be recruited. We'll test stimulating specific brain regions (rDLPFC or rIFG) to reduce negative emotional responses during stress. This will involve tDCS and sham stimulation while measuring physiological responses (skin conductance, heart rate, muscle activity) during a stress test. We'll also use tasks to measure impulse control after stimulation.

In the second phase, based on the first phase's findings, we'll recruit 40 adolescents (11-17 years) with self-harm behavior. We'll test whether multiple tDCS sessions combined with emotion regulation training (DBT-A skills training) reduce self-harm more effectively than training with sham stimulation. Participants will be followed up a month after the intervention.

Goal: The project aims to understand how brain stimulation can help reduce self-harm in adolescents and improve their overall well-being.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adolescents aged 11 to 17 years
• Willingness to participate in the experiment (informed consent from the patients and their legal guardians)
• Normal intelligence quotient (IQ) > 80
• Diagnosis of depression and a history of self-injurious behavior.
-	Depression is assessed using the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI-II)—a standardized depression questionnaire.
-	Self-injurious behavior is assessed using the SITBI-G questionnaire (German version) and a self-monitoring diary.
Exclusion criteria:
• IQ < 80
• Premature birth (before the 37th week of gestation)
• Birth weight < 2500 g
• Developmental disorder or neurological condition, particularly a history of epilepsy/epileptic seizures
• Family history of epileptic seizures
• History of traumatic brain injury with loss of consciousness
• Bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or currently reported suicidality, substance use, or regular medication use other than antidepressants
• Presence of a pacemaker or deep brain stimulation device, metal implants in the head or neck area, or other implants in the body
• History of cranial injury involving skull fracture or brain tissue damage
• Severe physical illness (affecting internal organs or metabolic disorders)
• Pregnancy or breastfeeding (for female participants)
• Acute dermatological conditions of the scalp
• Claustrophobia
• Contraindications for an MRI scan
